title: 悯农·其二
author: Li Shen

translation: Hoeing the crops under the noonday sun
Sweat drips onto the soil beneath the plants
Who knows that the food on your plate
Every grain comes from bitter toil

annotations.锄禾: to hoe the crops — farm work in the fields
annotations.当午: at noon, when the sun is strongest

appreciation: This poem is recited across China to teach children to respect food. The image of a farmer sweating under the noon sun makes every grain of rice feel earned. Its final line — 'every grain comes from bitter toil' — has become a proverb about cherishing the fruits of labor.
